name: xbench
intro: xbench是一个动态的、与职业对齐的评估套件，旨在弥合AI代理能力与现实世界生产力之间的差距。它通过行业专业人士定义的评估任务，针对具有商业意义的领域，创建与生产力价值强相关的指标。该框架能够预测技术-市场契合度（TMF），并随着时间的推移跟踪产品能力。初步实施包括招聘和营销两个基准，分别评估代理在真实业务场景中的能力。
build_method: 专家构建, 人工标注
scale: 招聘50个任务, 营销50个需求
intro_en: xbench is a dynamic, career-aligned evaluation suite designed to bridge the gap between AI agent capabilities and real-world productivity. It creates metrics highly correlated with productivity value through evaluation tasks defined by industry professionals, targeting commercially significant domains. The framework can predict Technology-Market Fit (TMF) and track product capabilities over time. Initial implementations include two benchmarks, recruiting and marketing, which assess agent performance in real business scenarios.

drawio_review_note: Aligned with xbench arXiv:2506.13651v1, Figures 1-6, Sections 3.1-3.3, Tables 1-7, Section 4.1, and Appendix A.1 Tables 11-17; official project https://xbench.org/. The website xbench_profession_v2.4.pdf is a standalone snapshot, not arXiv v2. Official repository https://github.com/xbench-ai/xbench-evals at inspected HEAD 17c562192cc7e62215bfb98b65e9f8806fb95504 does not publish the Recruitment/Marketing data, runner, parser, or scorer. Required conflicts: Section 3.2 prose versus Figure 4 swaps Recruitment 44/30/26 category bindings, and Section 3.3 prose versus Figure 6 swaps Marketing 68/16/16 bindings. Final aggregation and invalid-output rules are undisclosed.. xbench starts from expert workflow/time/importance interviews, filters tasks by feasibility and evaluability, collects live business demands, labels static/dynamic items, and records expert time/value for separate IRT/TMF analysis. Recruitment builds 50 cases across Company Mapping, People-to-Info, and Info-to-People; every branch passes a public-information solvability plus self-disclosed/reliable-source check, confirmed for all 50 cases, before the web-search agent runs. Marketing builds 50 anonymized campaigns from briefs, recommendation lists, and client selections, using 836 historical selected-influencer profiles to generate ideal-persona rubrics. Both branches use Gemini-2.5-Flash judges; profession parsers and final aggregation are not public.
